# Chapter 6: Flight Test

Eglin Air Force Base sprawled across the Florida panhandle like a city that had grown up around a single purpose, which was essentially what it was. The base covered over 700 square miles, making it one of the largest in the world, and its job was testing—weapons, vehicles, systems, the endless cycle of development that kept American military technology ahead of whatever adversaries the Cold War had produced.
